result.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
result.comment: Accepted at SLM-Agents: 1st Workshop on SLMs for Agentic Systems, NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种云端大模型写程序、设备端小模型在运行期解释用户数据的混合智能体架构，并在 AppWorld 上比较其与纯代码智能体、云端 ReAct 循环的成功率与数据本地性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「程序把对运行期数据的受限问题延后交给本地小模型」的调度方式，可能为 LVR 中何时让渡计算给低成本证据获取（LOOK）及相应收益-成本权衡提供类比线索，但任务与视觉表示无关，可供核查。
